issue_context.title: [Bug]: apps.plugin should expose metrics differently
issue_context.body:
### Bug description

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2662304/233591738-6477db00-3b90-4d08-96f9-92d05af4525a.png)

This chart of apps.plugin is fundamentally wrong. Each application monitored should be an instance.

For NIDL should be:

* Nodes
* Instances (applications, like web server, sql server, etc)
* Dimensions (system cpu time, user cpu time)
* Labels (at least application name should be there to allow grouping multiple instances of the same application)

### Expected behavior

One instance should be created for every application monitored.

So, the charts should be:

- `apps.cpu`, with dimensions `system` and `user`.
- `apps.physical.io`, with dimensions `reads` and `writes`.
- `apps.logical.io`, with dimensions `reads` and `writes`.
- `apps.file_descriptors`, with dimensions the different types of file descriptors the application has open (files, pipes, sockets, etc).
- `apps.mem` with dimension `used` and `shared`.
- `apps.mem.virtual` with dimensions `used`.
- `apps.mem.swap` with dimensions `used`.
- `apps.page_faults` with dimensions `minor` and `major`.
- `apps.processes` with dimensions `threads` and `processes`.
- `apps.uptime` with dimensions `uptime`.

Similarly for `users` (instance is the user) and `groups` (instance is the group).

### Steps to reproduce

Just use apps.plugin charts

### Installation method

kickstart.sh

### System info

```shell
Irrelevant.
```


### Netdata build info

```shell
Irrelevant
```


### Additional info

Related to #13347
